summary: 145 Tapestry of the Past 7 – The Gupta Era: An Age of Tireless Creativity Neither force nor mere diplomacy can eliminate evil; nor is righteousness upheld by flattery alone. It is wisdom and knowledge that truly strengthen a kingdom — not indulgence in luxuries. ­— Kālidāsa in Raghuvanśham The Gupta Era: An Age of Tireless Creativity CHAPTER 7 1. Why is the Gupta period sometimes called the ‘classical age’ in Indian history? What was happening in the rest of the subcontinent at this time? Who were some great figures of this period, and why do their stories matter today? Landscape of Ajanta caves, dating from the 2nd century BCE to about 480 CE 146 Exploring Society: India and Beyond | Grade 7 Part 1 Dhruv and Bhavisha had just returned from their journey to the Pānḍya kingdom. They had seen the splendid markets, taken a short trip on a ship, and met some Roman traders buying pearls. Now they were itching to use Itihāsa again and jump a few centuries. “What would that be like?” they wondered.
